metadata.name: R25 · level-2 wander by boredom + heading + avoidance — REGRESSION (§17.4): heading outweighs avoidance, 297 wall contacts/min; the arbitration question
metadata.description: Phase 1e of the intent boundary (design doc §16.4): the same module code one level up. The 'motors' are the three twist commands (vx, vy, vyaw) to Pollen's walking policy, the 'senses' are the body's own velocity from contact odometry and the gyro, normalised by the trained command ranges (0.4, 0.3, 1.0). Identification by held twist pulses (babble_hold 75 ticks = 1.5 s, scale 0.8 of range — above the walker's ~0.25 m/s standing regime), one motor at a time, alternating sign. Judged on the identified A: the velocity rows against the commands must be positive on the diagonal and dominant, per axis, against the walker's measured response (§16.2). No prior, no controller learning: identification only.
scaffolds_active: alpha_walking.onnx drives the joints throughout — the level-2 body; alpha_stand rescues falls

description: R25 (level-2 wander by boredom: the map's familiarity changes the heading the brain keeps; heading + avoidance priors), from a1v2_r24_l2_wander.json: Phase 2b, second probe (design doc §17.4): R24's surprise prior had no gradient (surprise is not a linear function of the command), so the map's familiarity gates the heading instead: when its surprise has sat below 0.8 of its own long average for --wander-bored seconds, the heading reference behind slot 10 jumps by --wander-turn degrees with a random sign and the heading prior (R22's) turns the body; novelty holds the heading. Avoidance priors kept. Judged on coverage against R23's nine cells, collisions, the map's growth, and the moved wall.
